itineraries.destination: Balkans roadtrip (Kosovo, North Macedonia, Montenegro; optional Albania add-on)

items.details: Fly into Pristina, described as a reasonably priced gateway into North Macedonia and Montenegro.

Rental car pickup; cross-border green card purchased at pickup for about $25. Kosovo rentals $30-40/day, Montenegro ~$70/day in high season; one-way drop-off ~$500 extra; full coverage ~$11/day extra.
items.name: Discover Cars

items.details: Lunch stop in Skopje at an unnamed restaurant overlooking the river, plus a walk through the Old Bazaar and over the Stone Bridge.
Self-guided wander through the Ottoman Old Bazaar, across the Stone Bridge to the neoclassical city center.
items.name: Skopje Old Bazaar and Stone Bridge walk

items.details: Lakefront hotel with included beach chairs and paddleboards, rooftop spa, breakfast, parking and pool. She recommends one night on the lake and one night near the Old Town.
items.name: Hotel Lago Ohrid

items.details: Paddle boards included with the hotel; calm morning water along the shoreline.
items.name: Paddle boarding on Lake Ohrid

items.details: Tandem paraglide over the lake and old town; flight itself only ~8 minutes after a long drive up into the mountains.
items.name: Paragliding above Lake Ohrid

items.details: Evening wandering the old town's stone alleys, viewpoints, churches and lakefront cafes.
items.name: Lake Ohrid Old Town exploration

items.details: One of three old-town spots she names (limoncello spritzes).
items.name: Limonce Bar

items.details: Named old-town cafe pick.
items.name: Cafe Liquid

items.details: Wine bar with a wide variety of local wines.
items.name: Wine Bar and Winery Mal Sv. Kliment

items.details: Full travel day: drive back, return the rental car, then bus onward to Prizren. She suggests dropping the car and busing rather than driving the whole way.
Her recommended hotel in Prizren; owner gave local recommendations and helped with parking in the pedestrian area.
items.name: Sapphire Hotel Prizren

items.details: Late-afternoon hike for panoramic views over the red rooftops, minarets and mountains.
items.name: Hike to Prizren Fortress

items.details: New restaurant/lounge/club popular with locals; reservation recommended for the patio.
items.name: Reception

items.details: Rooftop bar with city views.
items.name: Utopia Rooftop Bar

items.details: Optional Day 6 alternative: iron-pathway cliff climb in the mountains near Peja (cables, clips, harnesses). She lists it with no booking URL.
items.name: Via Ferrata in Peja

items.details: Optional guided alternative for the Peja day trip.
items.name: Full day nature and culture tour in Peja

items.details: Optional shorter guided alternative for the Peja day trip.
items.name: Peja and Rugova half day tour

items.details: Once-daily night bus (departs Pristina 5pm, stops in Prizren, transits Albania) to Budva, Montenegro; ~7-8 hours, no bathroom/wifi/outlets onboard, seats comfortable with rest stops. Border crossings into Albania and Montenegro were fast.
items.name: Vetoni Tourist night bus

items.details: Private boat along the Budva riviera: turquoise water, cliffs and hidden coves; she booked private to avoid summer crowds.
items.name: Private Budva boat tour
items.price_hint: $575 for a group of 4-5 for 4 hours

items.details: Beach club day: sun chair and umbrella; $7 water taxi alternative to Hawaii Island for quieter swimming beaches with three small beach bars.
items.name: Coco Beach Club

items.details: Evening walk through the medieval old town, best at sunset.
items.name: Budva Old Town stroll

items.details: Named restaurant pick in Budva Old Town.
items.name: Shanghai Sushi

items.details: Named restaurant pick in Budva Old Town.
items.name: Restaurant Mlin

items.details: 4-star hotel near the Old Town/Riviera (actual name not stated by the creator), about $100 per night.
Day trip by bus (~$7) rather than taxi (~$70); heavy traffic expected. She advises checking the cruise schedule and avoiding days with docked cruise ships.
Cable car over the Bay of Kotor; at the top she recommends the Aerobar (suspended panoramic bar) and the Falcon ride. Tickets must be bought in advance.
items.name: Kotor Cable Car

items.details: UNESCO-listed old town walk.
items.name: Kotor Old Town

items.details: Her top recommendation around the bay if choosing one stop: quieter waterfront town, reached by boat or car.
items.name: Perast

items.details: Underwater wine-aging barge she visited but found overpriced and unwelcoming; reservation required far in advance, water taxi ~$100 round trip or taxi ~$70, bottles from $55 (bottle only, no glasses). Included as a visited spot with her honest caveat.
items.name: Kraken Underwater Wine Cellar

items.details: Winery visit in Montenegro's wine region near Podgorica; she suggests hiring a driver or joining a wine tour rather than driving.
items.name: Mkenh Winery

items.details: Boutique-feel 5-star base for the wine region, about $110 including a la carte breakfast.
items.name: Hotel Hemera

itineraries.summary: Alyssa Ramos's 9-day luxury-adventure Balkans roadtrip: fly into Pristina, drive to Lake Ohrid in North Macedonia for paddle boarding and paragliding, return through Prizren in Kosovo with an optional Peja adventure day, then take the night bus to Montenegro for Budva's coast, a Kotor day trip with the cable car, and the wine country near Podgorica. An Albania detour (Tirana, Ksamil) is offered as an optional 2-3 day add-on.
itineraries.title: Ultimate Balkans Roadtrip Travel Guide for Luxury Adventurers

items.details: Casa particular near Plaza Mayor (specific casa not named); she also notes the Day 3 casa particular in Cienfuegos near Paseo del Prado is unnamed.
Colonial museum visit while walking Trinidad's cobblestone streets.
items.name: Museo Romantico

items.details: Parish church stop on the Trinidad walking route.
items.name: Iglesia Parroquial de la Santisima

items.details: Climb the bell tower for a panoramic view of the city.
items.name: Trinidad bell tower climb

items.details: Evening cultural activity followed by an authentic meal and a canchanchara (local cocktail).
items.name: Cooking lesson, salsa class or drum session

items.details: Famous nightclub inside a cave; she notes it is government-owned so U.S. citizens cannot go.
items.name: Disco Ayala

items.details: Guided hike arranged by a local agency (unnamed) through jungle and farmland to Valley of the Sugar Mills views, a waterfall and natural swimming pools; ends with lunch and a mojito at a jungle cafe.
items.name: Guided hike in Parque Guanayara

items.details: "Russian limousine" (old war truck) ride up the steep hill to the park entrance.
Guided kayak across the bay with a stop at Castillo de Jagua, an 18th-century fortress; guides share colonial history and pirate lore.
items.name: Guided kayaking tour on the Bay of Cienfuegos

items.details: 18th-century fortress guarding the bay entrance, reached by kayak.
items.name: Castillo de Jagua

items.details: Unnamed outdoor restaurant by the bay for lobster lunch: grilled lobster with garlic and lime, rice and plantains.
City square with neoclassical architecture and Teatro Tomas Terry, walk along Paseo del Prado to the Malecon and Punta Gorda's seaside mansions.
items.name: Parque Jose Marti and Paseo del Prado walk

itineraries.summary: Alyssa Ramos's 3-day Cuba itinerary: Day 1 exploring Trinidad's colonial center (Plaza Mayor, Museo Romantico, bell tower, evening cooking or salsa class), Day 2 hiking to waterfalls and natural pools in Parque Guanayara, Day 3 kayaking the Bay of Cienfuegos to Castillo de Jagua with a lobster lunch, then the city square and malecon. Casa particular stays throughout; written with U.S.-citizen travel notes.
itineraries.title: Best Things to Do in Trinidad and Cienfuegos: A 3-Day Cuba Itinerary

extractions.notes: Both itineraries are day-by-day guides from the creator's own blog (published 2026-08-24 and 2026-01-26 per WordPress API). Balkans guide calls itself a '9 Day' itinerary though only Days 1-8 are sectioned (Day 9 implied as departure); days recorded as 9 per the source's own title. Paragliding price: booking-link label says $128 while body text says ~$110; recorded $128 from the link label. One beach-club name near Lake Ohrid was redacted in the source text ('((((((((') and was not included. Budva hotel and all casa particular stays are unnamed in the source; recorded with null names. Via Ferrata in Peja is listed by the creator with no booking URL.
